title: Module-valued global sections and the normalized derived ringed-point adjunction
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a commutative ringed site, small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with R-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put A=Gamma(C,R), the ring of compatible families [def-sfb-coefficient-module-global-sections]. Define the A-module-valued sections functor Gamma_A by Hom_R(R,-), with pointwise global-scalar action, equivalently compatible families with evaluation at 1. It is additive and has the canonical left adjoint P; its universal property identifies P(M) with the sheafification of U maps to R(U) tensor_A M. Define its ordinary natural tensor comparison P(M tensor_A N) to P(M) tensor_R P(N) by requiring that its adjunct sends x tensor y to the tensor of the two unit sections, equivalently on local generators a tensor (x tensor y) maps to (a tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y). This unit formula uniquely fixes the comparison. Use the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the K-flat and total tensor constructions [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Pullback is additive and preserves the K-flat quasi-isomorphisms used to derive it, and sends flat-term K-flat complexes to flat-term K-flat complexes. Define LP by the K-flat left derived functor and RGamma_A by the K-injective right derived functor [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Define the unique adjunction LP left-adjoint to RGamma_A whose Hom bijection, after the derived comparison maps on source and target complexes, is the localization of the ordinary complex adjunction. For the derived tensor represented by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation] and the coefficient tensor/cohomology conventions [def-sfb-ringed-site-cohomology-tensor-maps], define the unique natural map LP(U tensor_A^L V) to T(LP(U),LP(V)) characterized on every pair of flat-term K-flat representatives by the ordinary tensor comparison, its total-complex comparison and the canonical left-derived counits. This canonical derived tensor comparison is an isomorphism. These are the module and derived adjunctions and tensor comparison of the canonical morphism of ringed topoi (Sh(C),R) to (Sh(pt),A); no final object of C is assumed.
